Definition: from G1176 and G1417; two and ten, i.e. twelve:--twelve.
BiblicalUsage: Twelve is the number of the tribes and the apostles, and this spelling of it never stands in the Greek New Testament: every occurrence of twelve is written with the single word for a dozen, and this compound form is a word-list entry with no verse to its name. I say so plainly, because no verse may be invented for it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the gap is honest: a word that never occurs still belongs in the record, and the twelve it names are real enough without it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
